Why do some injuries scar badly and others don't?

A lot of it has to do with the depth of the cut and the treatment during healing.

Scars are just connective tissue laid down instead of functional skin, because normally the basement layer - or the layer of skin which is regenerative - is damaged beyond being able to repair. As such, the injury is infiltrated with a cell called fibroblasts, which lays down the connective tissue meshwork.

If the injury isn't very deep, but improper care is taken to heal it, infection can cause the basement membrane to be damaged, and again it will not regrow. So after infection has waned fibroblasts will invade and fill in with connective tissue.

Keep in mind that different areas of your body have different superficial layer depths as well. Your heel for example is massively thick, while the skin on your hands is not.

When you open your file manager, and you click on the Network icon in the left-hand panel, does it populate with anything? Typically, if there are windows machines with a workgroup/domain and a master browser, you should see an icon for "Windows Network" in the main window. If that's not working, there may be a firewall issue or something else going on with your config. Need more info...

Try to list the shares from the Windows box at the command line. That should give us some useful feedback:

smbclient -U username -L hostname

Use a username with access to one or more shares on the Windows box, and of course the hostname of the target machine. If this times out, we know we have a network configuration issue somewhere.

  • run through Wine
  • run in a VM
  • dual boot
